definitions.explanation: Keio University ({慶應義塾大学|けいおうぎじゅくだいがく}), one of Japan's leading private universities. It grew from a school of Western learning that {福沢諭吉|ふくざわゆきち} opened in 1858.

examples.japanese: ⟦{姉|あね}→姉：00571_ane⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{慶応|けいおう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{卒業|そつぎょう}→卒業：01643_sotsugyou⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My older sister graduated from Keio.

examples.japanese: {慶応|けいおう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{学生|がくせい}→学生：00610_gakusei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧「{塾生|じゅくせい}」⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれる→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧。

{慶応|けいおう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{福沢諭吉|ふくざわゆきち}→福沢諭吉：31008_fukuzawayukichi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{開|ひら}いた→開く：01979_hiraku⟧⟦{塾|じゅく}→塾：04702_juku⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{始|はじ}まり→始まる：00841_hajimaru⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{代表|だいひょう}→代表：03419_daihyou⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧{私立大学|しりつだいがく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Keio began as a school opened by Fukuzawa Yukichi and is now one of Japan's leading private universities.

notes:
WRITING:
The university itself writes {慶應|けいおう}, with the old form of the second kanji; everyday writing often uses {慶応|けいおう}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {慶應義塾|けいおうぎじゅく}: the official name of the school and its whole system
- {慶大|けいだい}: the short form used in writing and headlines
- {早慶|そうけい}: Waseda and Keio together
- {塾生|じゅくせい}: a Keio student

ETYMOLOGY:
The school took its name from the {慶応|けいおう} era (1865–1868), the last era of the Edo period.
